title: Emile Christian's session with two trombones
summary: Mares gave Christian his own band session with Bob Havens, Harry Shields and Raymond Burke, which reviewers rated four stars.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from

yeah. Well, of course, in the later years, Emil went to bass. He gave up the trombone. But when I give this session to Emil, I had to have him on some trombone parts. So I got a good band back, Emil. I got Mike Lala, good trumpet man here, good lead trumpet man, and Harry Shields on clarinet, and Bob Havens, who's one of the real fine trombone players here around New Orleans today. Of course, Joe Cupero on banjo and Monk Hazel on drums, Armand Hug on piano. And I thought I would record a few tunes, and one or two of them I'd use two trombones. And this I did. Of course, naturally, I have a little tune I wrote called A Mardi Gras Parade. And we need a lot of tailgate, we need a lot of trombone. And I use Emil all the way through on trombone along with Bob Havens. And then we go on to a little tune called Lost My Heart in Dixieland, which was recorded by the original Dixieland band. Of course, Emil was a member of that band. And I used two trombones. And let me bring this out too, Bill. On this particular session, I used Harry Shields, but I bought Raymond Boykin. They also played two clarinets on two of the tunes. I think it, you always hurt the one you love. And also, I lost my heart in Dixieland. And of course, Raymond and Harry make a wonderful team together. And that came out marvelous. In fact, it's the reviewers give this four stars where anyone that reviews it, they think it's one of the finest things I've done.
So Christian only plays trombone on a couple of the numbers.

That's all. He plays on the Mardi Gras Parade all the way through. And then on the Lost My Heart in Dixieland, he takes a solo with Bob Havens. They take a two trombone solo. So Emil Christians is another one that I've had the good faith of and happy to say that I gave him a band also, that this old gent could also say that he had a band of his own for his family or from years to come, you know, that he had something to a band of his own.
